outcome: cesarean delivery (CD) due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate (NRFHR)
neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rates
cohort: The study included 432 pregnancies with fetal growth restriction (estimated fetal weight < 10th percentile) undergoing induction of labor, stratified by pathological or normal cerebroplacental ratio.
finding: In FGR pregnancies undergoing induction of labor, isolated pathological CPR was not associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery for NRFHR, but was linked to higher NICU admission rates and lower birthweights.
mod_finding: Isolated pathological CPR was not associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery (overall or due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate) in FGR pregnancies undergoing induction of labor.
birth_weight: 2174 ± 279 g for pathological CPR group, 2279 ± 278 g for normal CPR group
gest_age: 37.1 weeks for pathological CPR group, 38.0 weeks for normal CPR group
